record.title: Norway restricts Russian road-transport undertakings at Storskog, April 2022
record.scope: Norwegian road-carrier prohibition with documented application to the Storskog route toward Tromsø and Barentsburg.
record.direction: Russian-carrier road goods transport into Norway; the underlying national rule is broader than this observed route
record.movement: Non-exempt road-transport undertakings established in Russia
record.exceptions: Specified journeys begun before 29 April have conditional grace through 7 May; universal mail and authorised specified goods remain excepted. Unrestricted carriage by a different eligible operator is not the same cohort.
record.enforcement: E24 and the foreign ministry describe Russian carriers being stopped and the Norwegian-carrier workaround.
record.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified in this round.
record.relationship: No matching Russian road-undertaking episode appears in the frozen northern inventory or R01–R21 additions. EU010 and the October 2023 car-import proposal concern different persons/vehicles and later dates.
record.status_observation: Historical source evidence only. Unknown endpoint does not establish the present status of the border.
record.current_timing: Formal policy: confirmed through 2022-07-06; at least 68 calendar-day difference; reopening unknown
record.current_corrections: Goods carried by a Norwegian operator later passed; that is not a reopening for Russian-established carriers. The final carrier-rule endpoint remains unknown.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: Codes describe the attributed purposes of the specified restriction, not all policies at the same border.

followup_reviews.Separate challenger: rounds_protocol, separate same-model challenge of both original halves; prior involvement disclosed
followup_reviews.Research finding: Occurrence and inclusion remain supported for the April 2022 Russian road-undertaking prohibition, distinct from the later passenger-car rule and maritime port ban. Keep Russian-established road carriers as the restricted cohort. Pre-existing journeys, mail and authorised goods have exceptions. Supplies subsequently carried by a Norwegian operator do not establish return of Russian carriers. P1 retains formal onset 29 April 2022, confirmation through 6 July and a 68-calendar-day policy lower bound. The 7 May conditional grace is not a universal onset; the Norwegian-carrier workaround is not an endpoint. Retain the attributed sanctions rationale from the Norwegian government’s explicit statement about pressure and financing of the war. The policy notice was freshly read. E24 was reread from preserved full text and quotes ministry spokeswoman Ane Lunde, with NRK first reporting the solution; the common government origin is explicit. The documented Storskog route remains unlocated. No mainland perimeter or Svalbard border closure is inferred from the onward freight destination.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge
followup_reviews.Challenge finding: Challenge packet SHA-256: c6e6fa17f0d3353c233102eec4583df128ecbb23a0ee9696770f763c8bafc444. Per-question challenge findings remain in that packet.
followup_reviews.Root decision: Accept16full-current-domain assessments with unresolved findings retained and seven guarded native changes: one observed-reopening flag, three Argentine cohort summaries and three phase-specific labels. Retain all dates and numerical durations, all held/incomplete phases, exceptions and unlocated geography. Accept14source-metadata refinements without expanding evidence claims.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: REC50-R30-NQ02 — Final carrier-specific lifting and permissions remain unresolved; an eligible Norwegian carrier’s passage cannot close the Russian-carrier interval.
